mainTopic: Modesty in intimacy, five dangerous actions, the ban on daytime intimacy, checking cloths, and the טומאה of snow
overview: This amud finishes רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list of behaviors הקב״ה hates with two items about modesty in the bedroom. שמואל explains that 'any living being' means people such as slaves, not mice, and the גמרא tells how great אמוראים guarded their privacy. רבי שמעון בן יוחי then lists five dangerous actions, and the גמרא explains each one: peeled foods and diluted drinks left overnight, sleeping in a cemetery, throwing cut nails in public, and intimacy right after bloodletting. Next, רב חסדא and רב הונא forbid intimacy by day, and רבא allows it in the dark. The גמרא defends this ban against three sources by reading each one as talking about examining (בדיקה), not intimacy. That leads to a discussion of which cloths may be used for checking: linen, soft wool, and certain kinds of flax. Finally, the גמרא explains how snow works for טומאה, and אביי shows how a whole lump of snow can become טמא through the airspace of an earthenware oven.

steps.title: The last two items on the list of hated behaviors
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list ends with urinating naked in front of one's bed and marital relations in front of any living being.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who urinates naked in front of his bed, and one who has marital relations in front of any living being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list that started just before this text: things רבי שמעון בן יוחי says הקב״ה hates. Here are the last two items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items are about צניעות, modesty in the bedroom. The phrase 'any living being' is very broad, and the next step asks how far it really goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Has marital relations (a polite phrase, literally 'uses his bed')
In front of any living being

phrases.english: and one who urinates naked in front of his bed,
and one who has marital relations in front of any living being.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of hated behaviors from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urinating naked before one's bed and marital relations in front of any living being are hated behaviors.

steps.title: Does this include even mice?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks שמואל whether 'any living being' includes even mice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to שמואל: Even in front of mice?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks a clarifying question about the last item: how far does 'any living being' go?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, 'any living being' would include tiny creatures like mice, which are almost always around. That would make the rule nearly impossible to keep, so רב יהודה asks whether it really means that.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to Shmuel:
Even in front of mice?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לִשְׁמוּאֵל וַאֲפִילּוּ לִפְנֵי עַכְבָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how wide the phrase 'any living being' is
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'any living being' includes even small creatures like mice

steps.title: No, it means people such as slaves
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that mice are not included; the rule refers to a certain household that had relations in front of their slaves and maidservants.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Sharp one, no! Rather, it means a case like so-and-so's household, who have relations in front of their slaves and maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers: the rule is not about mice. It is about doing this in front of people, like one household that did it in front of their slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So 'any living being' is not meant in the widest sense. The real concern is people who can see and understand, and שמואל gives a real example of a family that ignored this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sharp one', שמואל's nickname for רב יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: 'Any living being' is not about mice. It means people, even slaves.

phrases.english: He said to him: Sharp one, no!
phrases.notes: Literally 'sharp-toothed one', a friendly nickname שמואל used for his student רב יהודה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like the case of so-and-so's household,
who have marital relations in front of their slaves and maidservants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mice are not included; the rule means people, such as slaves and maidservants.

steps.title: What were they relying on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning that household used to allow this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those people, what did they learn from a פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source that household thought permitted them to act this way. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes this family was not simply careless; they must have had a reason, a דרשה. The question asks what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they learn from a פסוק?

phrases.english: And those people, what did they learn from a verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the household mentioned by שמואל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What פסוק that household relied on to permit relations in front of slaves

steps.title: A people compared to a donkey
steps.stepSummary: They read 'stay here with the donkey' as 'a people like a donkey,' treating slaves like animals in front of whom privacy is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Stay here with the donkey': a people that is like a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the household's source: a play on words in a פסוק about אברהם's servants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עִם (with) is read as עַם (a people), so the servants are 'a people like a donkey.' The household reasoned that, just as one may be private in front of an animal, one may be in front of slaves. The גמרא presents this as their reasoning, but this behavior is one of the hated things on the list, and שמואל gave it as his example of 'in front of any living being.'
steps.confusionAlert: This דרשה is what that household relied on. It does not make their behavior right; it is listed among the things הקב״ה hates.

phrases.english: "Stay here with the donkey"
a people that is similar to a donkey.
phrases.notes: They read עִם (with) as עַם (a people), so the servants are compared to the donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the household's source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They read 'with the donkey' as 'a people like a donkey,' treating slaves like animals.

steps.title: How the אמוראים guarded their privacy
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rang the bells of his bed canopy, אביי chased away flies, and רבא chased away gnats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא would ring the bells of the canopy; אביי would chase away flies; רבא would chase away gnats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how three great אמוראים were careful about privacy before marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא rang bells so people would know to stay away. אביי and רבא went even further and chased away flies and gnats, though the law did not require it, as שמואל said about mice.

keyTerms.meaning: Bells of the canopy over the bed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that great people went beyond the strict rule (which excludes small creatures) out of extra modesty.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מְקַרְקֵשׁ זָגֵי דְּכִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna would ring the bells of the canopy,
phrases.notes: The canopy hung over his bed; the bells signaled others to keep away.

phrases.english: Abaye would chase away flies,
Rava would chase away gnats.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מְקַרְקֵשׁ זָגֵי דְּכִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples of sages' practices about privacy in relations
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sages took extra steps to ensure privacy, even from insects.

steps.title: Five dangerous actions
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי lists five actions so dangerous that whoever does them is responsible for his own death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי said: There are five things that whoever does them is liable for his life and his blood is on his own head: eating peeled garlic, a peeled onion or a peeled egg, or drinking diluted drinks, that were left overnight; sleeping in a cemetery; cutting one's nails and throwing them into a public area; and letting blood and then having marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי gives a new list: five actions that put a person in danger, so he is to blame if harm comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group is foods and drinks that were peeled or diluted and left overnight. Then come sleeping in a cemetery, throwing cut nails into a public place, and relations right after bloodletting. 'His blood is on his head' means he brought the danger on himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts his own life at risk, is liable for his life
His blood is on his own head (he is to blame)

steps.whatToRemember: Five dangers: peeled garlic/onion/egg or diluted drinks left overnight, sleeping in a cemetery, throwing nails in public, and relations right after bloodletting.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Left overnight' goes on all the foods and drinks, not just the drinks.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said:
There are five things that whoever does them
is liable for his life, and his blood is on his own head:
one who eats peeled garlic,
or a peeled onion, or a peeled egg,
and one who drinks diluted drinks
that were left overnight,
phrases.notes: This goes back on all the items: the garlic, onion, egg and drinks.

phrases.english: and one who sleeps in a cemetery,
and one who cuts his nails and throws them into a public area,
and one who lets blood and then has marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי חֲמִישָּׁה דְּבָרִים הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new list from the same sage, on dangerous actions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five actions put a person at risk of death, and he is responsible for the outcome.

steps.title: Peeled garlic is dangerous even when sealed in a basket
steps.stepSummary: Peeled garlic, onion or egg left overnight is dangerous even if it was tied and sealed in a basket, because a רוח רעה rests on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats peeled garlic, and so on: even if the peeled items were put in a basket, tied up and sealed, an evil spirit rests on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the first item on רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list, peeled garlic. It says that closing it up does not protect it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the danger comes from something getting into the food at night, so sealing it would help. The גמרא says no. The danger is a רוח רעה, and a sealed basket does not keep that out.

phrases.english: One who eats peeled garlic, etc.
And even though they are placed in a basket
and tied up and sealed
an evil spirit rests upon them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first item in רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Peeled garlic, onion or egg left overnight is dangerous even when sealed, because a רוח רעה rests on it.

steps.title: No danger if roots or peel were left on
steps.stepSummary: The danger only applies when nothing was left on the food. If some root or peel remained, there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he left nothing of their roots or their peel on them. But if he left their roots or their peel on them, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on the peeled-food rule. A little root or peel left on the food takes away the danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 made the rule stronger, since even a sealed basket does not help. This step narrows it. The danger is only for food that is completely bare, with no root or peel at all.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when (introduces a limit on a rule)
we have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: Peeled foods left overnight are dangerous even if sealed, but not if some root or peel was left on.

phrases.english: And we only said this

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא שִׁיֵּיר בָּהֶן עִיקָּרָן אוֹ קְלִיפָּתָן,
phrases.english: when he did not leave on them their roots or their peel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שִׁיֵּיר בָּהֶן עִיקָּרָן אוֹ קְלִיפָּתָן
phrases.english: but if he left on them their roots or their peel
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא שִׁיֵּיר בָּהֶן עִיקָּרָן אוֹ קְלִיפָּתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the peeled-food danger described in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If any root or peel remains on the food, there is no danger.

steps.title: Diluted drinks are only dangerous in metal vessels
steps.stepSummary: The next item is diluted drinks left overnight. שמואל says this is only dangerous when they sat overnight in metal vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who drinks diluted drinks that were left overnight: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, this is only when they stayed overnight in metal vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item on the list, diluted drinks left overnight. שמואל limits the danger to drinks kept in metal vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list itself does not say anything about the container. שמואל adds that condition, so a diluted drink left overnight in another kind of vessel is not part of this danger.

phrases.english: And one who drinks diluted drinks
that were left overnight.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is only when they stayed overnight in metal vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second item in רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Diluted drinks left overnight are only dangerous when they were kept in metal vessels.

steps.title: נתר vessels count like metal vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that vessels made of נתר are treated like metal vessels for this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: נתר vessels are considered like metal vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא makes שמואל's rule a little wider by adding one more kind of container.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל named only metal vessels. רב פפא says that נתר vessels belong in the same group, so drinks left overnight in them are also dangerous.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And natron vessels are considered like metal vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens שמואל's metal-vessel condition to include נתר vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נתר vessels are treated like metal vessels for the overnight-drink danger.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also says the danger is only in metal vessels, and that נתר vessels count like metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבי יוחנן: this is only when they stayed overnight in metal vessels, and נתר vessels are considered like metal vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן, who agrees fully with both שמואל and רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule here. A second major אמורא saying the same thing shows that the metal-vessel limit and the נתר addition are widely accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: and likewise (shows agreement with what came before)
this is only when (introduces a condition)

steps.whatToRemember: Diluted drinks left overnight are only dangerous in metal or נתר vessels.

phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Yochanan:
This is only when they stayed overnight in metal vessels,
and natron vessels are considered like metal vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 10 and 11 with matching wording from רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן agrees: the danger applies only to metal vessels, and נתר vessels count like metal.

steps.title: Sleeping in a cemetery on purpose
steps.stepSummary: Sleeping in a cemetery is dangerous when it is done on purpose to have a רוח טומאה rest on oneself, because the spirits sometimes harm the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who sleeps in a cemetery: this means he does it so that a spirit of impurity will rest on him. Sometimes they put him in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third item on the list. The danger is when a person sleeps in a cemetery on purpose to draw a spirit to himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list only says 'one who sleeps in a cemetery.' The גמרא defines the case as someone who goes there with that goal. It also gives the reason: the spirits there can sometimes hurt him.

keyTerms.meaning: one who sleeps or stays overnight

phrases.english: And one who sleeps in a cemetery
in order that a spirit of impurity should rest on him,
sometimes they endanger him.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the spirits found in the cemetery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַלָּן בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה עָלָיו רוּחַ טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the third item in רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping in a cemetery to draw a רוח טומאה is dangerous, because the spirits may harm the sleeper.

steps.title: Why throwing cut nails in public is dangerous
steps.stepSummary: Throwing cut nails into a public area is dangerous because a pregnant woman might pass over them and miscarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who cuts his nails and throws them into a public area: this is because a pregnant woman may pass over them and miscarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item on רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list, throwing cut nails into a public area, and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the danger the גמרא names is not to the person who cuts the nails but to someone else: a pregnant woman who walks over them.

phrases.english: And one who cuts his nails
and throws them into a public area

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאִשָּׁה מְעוּבֶּרֶת עוֹבֶרֶת עֲלֵיהֶן וּמַפֶּלֶת.
phrases.english: because a pregnant woman may pass over them and miscarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing cut nails in public is dangerous because a pregnant woman passing over them may miscarry.

steps.title: Three suggested limits on the nail rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests three limits: the danger applies only with scissors, only when cutting both hand and foot nails, and only when nothing else was cut afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he cut them with scissors. And we only said this when he cut the nails of his hands and of his feet. And we only said this when he did not cut anything after them. But if he cut something after them, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three conditions that would make the nail danger much narrower. This sets up the next step, where they will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'ולא אמרן' line adds one more condition that must be met before there is danger. Under this approach, if any one condition is missing, such as cutting something else afterward, there is no concern.

keyTerms.meaning: his own (here, the nails of his hands)

phrases.english: And we only said this when he cuts them with scissors,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּשָׁקֵיל דִּידֵיהּ וּדְכַרְעֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and we only said this when he cuts those of his hands and of his feet,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא גַּז מִידֵּי בָּתְרַיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and we only said this when he did not cut anything after them,
but if he cut something after them
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the nail rule from step 14 with three conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: the nail danger applies only with scissors, only for hand and foot nails together, and only when nothing else was cut afterward.

steps.title: We worry about cut nails in every case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the three limits and says we are concerned about cut nails in every situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. We are concerned about the whole matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects all three limits from the previous step and concludes that we worry about cut nails in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא היא' means the opinion just stated is not accepted. The nail danger stays fully in force. Using scissors or not, hand and foot or not, cutting something afterward or not, we still worry.

keyTerms.meaning: but that is not so (rejects the previous view)

steps.whatToRemember: The three limits on the nail rule are rejected. Cut nails should not be thrown into a public area in any case.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop reading at step 15 and think the limits are the הלכה. 'ולא היא' cancels all three of them.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
we are concerned about the whole matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects all three limits proposed in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: All three suggested limits on the nail rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The limits make the danger too narrow; the concern applies in every case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We are concerned about throwing cut nails into a public area in all cases.

steps.title: Three ways to get rid of cut nails
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא ranks three ways of getting rid of cut nails: burning is the best, burying is good, and throwing them away is wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Three things were said about nails. One who burns them is pious, one who buries them is righteous, and one who throws them away is wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic of cut nails with a ברייתא that grades how a person disposes of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the danger mentioned earlier, that a pregnant woman might pass over thrown nails. Burning gets rid of them completely, so it is the top level, a חסיד. Burying is good, a צדיק, while throwing them where people walk is called רשע because it puts others at risk.

keyTerms.meaning: A pious person who goes beyond what is required
A righteous person who does what is proper

steps.whatToRemember: Burn your cut nails (best), bury them (good), but never just throw them away (wicked).

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Three things were said about nails:
One who burns them is pious,
one who buries them is righteous,
one who throws them away is wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּצִּפׇּרְנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of cut nails, after the גמרא said in step 16 that we worry about them in every case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning nails is pious, burying them is righteous, and throwing them away is wicked.

steps.title: Why intimacy after bloodletting is dangerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the last item on רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list and explains it: intimacy right after bloodletting leads to weak children, and if both spouses let blood, to children with ראתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who lets blood and has intimacy': as the Master said, one who lets blood and then has intimacy will have weak children. If both of them let blood and then had intimacy, he will have children afflicted with ראתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last danger from רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list and explains it with a saying of 'the Master'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletting weakens the body, so a child conceived right afterward will be weak. If both husband and wife let blood, the harm is worse, and the children may have a serious disease called ראתן.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lets blood, a common medical practice then
People afflicted with ראתן, a serious disease

phrases.english: "And one who lets blood and has intimacy":
as the Master said:
One who lets blood and has intimacy
will have weak children.
If both of them let blood and had intimacy,
he will have children afflicted with ראתן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמַּקִּיז דָּם וּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ — דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with nails, the גמרא moves to the last danger on רבי שמעון בן יוחי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intimacy right after bloodletting produces weak children. If both spouses let blood, the children may have ראתן.

steps.title: Eating something removes the danger
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the danger: it applies only if the person ate nothing after bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: We said this only when he did not taste anything. But if he tasted something, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב narrows the rule from the previous step so that it covers only a person who has not eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger comes from the weakness after bloodletting. Eating something restores strength, so once the person has eaten, intimacy is no longer a concern.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a phrase that limits a rule)
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא טְעֵים מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: We said this only when he did not taste anything,
but if he tasted something,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא טְעֵים מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the bloodletting danger from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bloodletting danger applies only if he ate nothing afterward.

steps.title: No intimacy during the day
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that intimacy during the day is forbidden and brings the פסוק 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is forbidden for a person to have intimacy by day, as it says: 'And you shall love your fellow as yourself.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: רב חסדא forbids intimacy during the day and gives a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The connection between the פסוק and the rule is not clear yet. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks how the פסוק teaches this.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is forbidden for a person
to have intimacy by day,
as it says: "And you shall love your fellow as yourself."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אָסוּר לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁיְּשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that is still about intimacy, but no longer about the dangers list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intimacy during the day is forbidden, based on 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך'.

steps.title: How does the verse teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'love your fellow' teaches a ban on intimacy by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the link is between the פסוק and רב חסדא's rule. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about loving other people and does not mention intimacy or daytime. The גמרא wants to see how one leads to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the implication? How does this show it?

phrases.english: How is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the source רב חסדא gave in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' leads to a ban on daytime intimacy.

steps.title: He might see something that turns him off
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that in daylight the husband may see something unpleasant in his wife, she may become repulsive to him, and that would harm his love for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Perhaps he will see something unattractive in her, and she will become repulsive to him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by showing how daytime intimacy could damage the husband's love for his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה to love your fellow includes your wife. If daylight exposes something unattractive, he might come to dislike her, which goes against the פסוק. Avoiding daytime intimacy protects that love.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Perhaps he will see something unattractive in her
and she will become repulsive to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שֶׁמָּא יִרְאֶה בָּהּ דָּבָר מְגוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Daylight may expose something that makes her repulsive to him, which would undermine his love for her and break 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך'.

steps.title: A reason from holiness
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says Jews are holy and therefore do not have intimacy by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Jews are holy, and they do not have intimacy by day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a different reason for avoiding intimacy by day, based on holiness and modesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's reason, as אביי explained it, is about protecting the husband's love. רב הונא instead presents it as a matter of the holiness of the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Jews are holy,
and they do not have intimacy by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different basis for the practice discussed by רב חסדא in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because Jews are holy, they do not have intimacy by day.

steps.title: When daytime intimacy is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits daytime intimacy in a dark house, and a תלמיד חכם may make it dark with his garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the house was dark, it is permitted. And a תלמיד חכם may make it dark with his garment and have intimacy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives exceptions to the ban on daytime intimacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is daylight, so darkness removes it. A dark house is enough for anyone. A תלמיד חכם, who is trusted to act modestly, may even create darkness by covering with his garment.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes it dark with his garment

steps.whatToRemember: Intimacy by day is forbidden, but it is allowed in a dark house, and a תלמיד חכם may make it dark with his garment.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And if the house was dark, it is permitted,
and a Torah scholar may make it dark with his garment and have intimacy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְאִם הָיָה בַּיִת אָפֵל — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ban on daytime intimacy from steps 20 and 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daytime intimacy is permitted in a dark house, and a תלמיד חכם may make it dark with his garment.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to allow intimacy by lamplight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ban on intimacy in the light from the משנה's words 'or she should be intimate by the light of a lamp.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'Or she should be intimate by the light of a lamp!' So intimacy in the light seems to be allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה that seems to allow intimacy in the light. That clashes with the rulings we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא and רב הונא said intimacy in the light is not allowed. Here the משנה itself seems to tell a woman to be intimate by lamplight. If the משנה says this, how can it be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: She should be intimate (a polite word for marital relations)
By the light of a lamp

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna: Or she should be intimate by the light of a lamp!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rulings in steps 20 and 23 that forbid intimacy in the light.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on intimacy by day or in the light (רב חסדא, רב הונא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to tell a woman to be intimate by lamplight, so it cannot be forbidden.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'she should examine by lamplight'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה should be read as talking about examining by lamplight, not intimacy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'She should examine by the light of a lamp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה differently. It is about checking herself by lamplight, not about intimacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the line is about checking for blood (בדיקה), it says nothing about whether intimacy in the light is allowed. So the ban stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
She should examine (check herself for blood)

steps.confusionAlert: אֵימָא here does not mean the משנה is wrong. The גמרא is telling us how to read the line: the word is about checking, not intimacy.

phrases.english: Say: She should examine by the light of a lamp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows intimacy by lamplight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about examining by lamplight.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show the משנה really means intimacy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens 'Even though they said one who is intimate by lamplight is disgraceful...'. That opening shows the ruling that follows is about intimacy by lamplight, against the rereading in step 26.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Even though they said that one who is intimate by the light of a lamp is disgraceful...' and yet בית שמאי still say she should be intimate by lamplight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on our משנה that opens 'Even though they said intimacy by lamplight is disgraceful...'. This seems to prove that the משנה's words really are about intimacy, so step 26's answer looks wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'even though they said' lead into a 'nevertheless': even though intimacy by lamplight is called disgraceful, בית שמאי still say she should be intimate by lamplight. That contrast only makes sense if the משנה really means intimacy, so the rereading 'examine' from step 26 seems not to work.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: Come and hear: Even though they said:
One who is intimate by the light of a lamp
is disgraceful!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on intimacy in the light
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that even though intimacy by lamplight is disgraceful, בית שמאי nevertheless require it, which shows the משנה really speaks of intimacy by lamplight and not of examining.

steps.title: Read it as examining by lamplight being disgraceful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the same way: the ברייתא is about one who examines by lamplight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'One who examines by the light of a lamp is disgraceful.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer as before. The ברייתא is about checking by lamplight, not intimacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the ברייתא's opening says that examining by lamplight is disgraceful, since the light may not be good enough. Even so, the משנה requires her to examine by lamplight. Now nothing speaks of intimacy in the light, so the ban is not challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: One who examines with regard to intimacy (checks before or after)

phrases.english: Say: One who examines regarding intimacy by the light of a lamp
is disgraceful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 with the same method as step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'even though' opening shows the משנה is about intimacy by lamplight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about examining by lamplight.

steps.title: The household of King מונבז was intimate by day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא praises the household of מונבז המלך for three practices, one of which was being intimate by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The household of King מונבז did three things, and they are mentioned with praise. They were intimate by day, they examined with white wool from פרהבא, and they kept the rules of impurity and purity with snow. In any case it teaches: they were intimate by day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third, stronger source. A ברייתא praises a royal family for being intimate by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source does not just allow daytime intimacy. It praises it. The גמרא focuses only on the first practice and sets the other two aside, which is what קתני מיהא, 'in any case it teaches,' means.

keyTerms.meaning: For praise, in a favorable way
Fine white wool from פרהבא, used for checking
In any case it teaches (focus only on this point)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְשֶׁל בֵּית מוֹנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ
phrases.english: Come and hear: And those of the household of King Munbaz
would do three things,
and they are mentioned with praise:
they would be intimate by day,
and they would examine regarding intimacy with wool of Parhava,
and they would keep impurity and purity with snow.
In any case it teaches: they would be intimate by day!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְשֶׁל בֵּית מוֹנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third and stronger challenge after steps 25 and 27 were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on intimacy by day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא praises a family for being intimate by day, so it must be allowed and even good.

steps.title: Read it as examining by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the household of מונבז examined by day, not that they were intimate by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'They would examine regarding intimacy by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer a third time. The praise is for checking in daylight, not for intimacy in daylight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking in daylight is more accurate than checking by a lamp. So praising them for it makes sense, and the ban on daytime intimacy stays in place.

phrases.english: Say: They would examine regarding intimacy by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 with the same method as steps 26 and 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The household of מונבז was praised for daytime intimacy.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were praised for examining by day.

steps.title: It makes sense: would intimacy be praised?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading: if the ברייתא meant intimacy by day, why would it be mentioned with praise?
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, it makes sense. If you think it means 'they were intimate,' would they be mentioned with praise for that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason to show its rereading is correct. It argues that daytime intimacy is not something you would praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if daytime intimacy were allowed, it does not seem like a special good deed. Since the ברייתא praises these practices, it must be talking about something praiseworthy, like careful checking.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (a support for what was just said)
If it enters your mind, if you would think

phrases.english: So too it makes sense,
for if you would think it means 'they were intimate,'
would they be mentioned with praise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא means 'examined by day'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own words 'mentioned with praise,' which do not seem to fit daytime intimacy

steps.title: Daytime intimacy can also be praiseworthy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the support: yes, daytime intimacy could be praised, because at night tiredness may cause the husband to reject his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is so. Because at night there is the pull of sleep, she may become unappealing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of the last step. It shows a real reason why daytime intimacy could deserve praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night the husband may be worn out and sleepy, so he might turn away from his wife. Being intimate by day avoids this, and that is a good reason for praise. So the argument 'it would not be praised' does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: She becomes unappealing in his eyes

steps.whatToRemember: Each source that seemed to allow intimacy in the light was read as talking about examining instead. The attempt to prove the last reading from the word 'praise' was pushed away, because daytime intimacy can be praiseworthy too.
steps.confusionAlert: This step only pushes away the 'it makes sense' support from step 31. The question is whether the praise proves the ברייתא meant examining.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
for since there is the pull of sleep,
she becomes unappealing to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support offered in step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the support from the word 'praise' in step 31
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Daytime intimacy can be praiseworthy, because nighttime tiredness may cause the husband to reject his wife.

steps.title: Checking with fine wool supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the household of מונבז checked with fine wool, which supports שמואל's rule that only linen or soft clean wool may be used for checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said they checked their beds with fine wool from פרהבא. This supports שמואל, who said one may check the bed only with linen or with clean, soft wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another part of the ברייתא about מונבז and shows that it backs up a rule of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes what the household actually did: they checked with soft wool. שמואל gives a rule that only linen or clean, soft wool may be used. The practice of this praised household fits his rule, so it serves as support.

keyTerms.meaning: they check, meaning they examine with a cloth for any sign of blood
bed; here a polite way of referring to intimacy

phrases.english: And they would examine their beds with wool of Parhava
phrases.notes: "Beds" is a polite way of talking about intimacy. They checked with a cloth before and after.

phrases.english: This supports Shmuel,
as Shmuel said:
One may not examine the bed
except with linen
or with clean, soft wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the debate about daytime intimacy to another detail in the same ברייתא of מונבז.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that checking may be done only with linen or clean, soft wool
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's report that the household of מונבז checked with fine wool of Parhava

steps.title: רב finally understands a saying he heard
steps.stepSummary: רב says this rule explains a strange saying he heard on Friday nights: "Who needs linen for bread?"
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This explains what I heard when I was there on Friday nights. People would call out, "Who needs linen for bread?" and I did not know what they meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב shares a memory. Now that he knows linen is used for checking, he understands a phrase people used to say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Friday night was a usual time for intimacy, and "bread" was a polite code word for it. People were offering linen cloths for checking. This shows that linen really was the standard material for a בדיקה, which fits שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday nights, the evenings of שבת
bread; here a polite code word for intimacy
this is what was meant by

phrases.english: Rav said:
This is what was meant when I was there
on Shabbat evenings, they would say:
"Who needs linen for bread?"
phrases.notes: "Bread" is a polite code word for intimacy.

phrases.english: and I did not know what they were saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב היינו דכי הואי התם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a real-life example showing that linen was used for checking, which fits שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Linen cloths for checking were commonly offered on Friday nights, showing that linen was the accepted material.

steps.title: רבא: worn-out flax is good for checking
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that worn-out flax cloths are good for a בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Worn-out flax cloths are good for checking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another material that may be used for checking: old, worn flax cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we heard only linen and soft wool. רבא widens the list to include old flax cloths. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:
These worn-out flax cloths
are good for examination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of which materials may be used for checking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Old, worn flax cloths are acceptable for a בדיקה.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids checking with flax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a ברייתא of דבי מנשה that says one may not check with flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the school of מנשה taught: One may not check the bed with a red cloth, a black cloth, or flax, only with linen or clean, soft wool!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule, because a ברייתא clearly lists flax as forbidden for checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said flax is good for checking. The ברייתא of דבי מנשה says flax may not be used. These seem to contradict each other directly.
steps.confusionAlert: פשתן and כיתנא are the same thing, flax: one is Hebrew and one is Aramaic. That is why this is a real contradiction. Also, פקולין, which is allowed, is a fine kind of linen and is not the same as plain flax here.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But the school of Menashe taught:
One may not examine the bed

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּעֵד אֱדוֹם, וְלֹא בְּעֵד שָׁחוֹר,
phrases.english: not with a red cloth, nor with a black cloth,
nor with flax,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּפָקוֹלִין אוֹ בְּצֶמֶר נָקִי וְרַךְ!
phrases.english: but only with linen or with clean, soft wool!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement from step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that worn flax cloths are good for checking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא of דבי מנשה explicitly forbids checking with flax, which contradicts רבא.

steps.title: Raw flax versus flax garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא forbids raw flax, while רבא allows cloths made from flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, the ברייתא, is about raw flax. That one, רבא, is about flax garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about different kinds of flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw flax fibers are not good for checking, so the ברייתא forbids them. Finished flax cloth is fine, which is what רבא meant. Both sources are correct, each about something different.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about flax itself,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא of דבי מנשה, which speaks of raw flax.

phrases.english: that is about flax garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא הא בכיתנא הא במאני דכיתנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source speaks about a different form of flax
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both sources were talking about the same flax.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids raw flax; רבא allows flax garments.

steps.title: Second answer: new versus worn flax garments
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: both sources speak of flax garments, but the ברייתא means new ones and רבא means worn ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: both are about flax garments. This one is about new garments, and that one is about worn-out garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to solve the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sources talk about flax cloth. New flax cloth is not good for checking, so the ברייתא forbids it. Old, worn flax cloth is good, and רבא said exactly "worn-out" (שחקי).

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (introduces a second answer)

steps.whatToRemember: For checking: linen or clean, soft wool is good. Flax is a problem, except for flax garments (first answer), or only worn-out flax garments (second answer).

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that are about flax garments;
this is about new ones, that is about worn-out ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואיבעית אימא הא והא במאני דכיתנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different split of cases: new versus worn garments
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the only way to answer is raw flax versus garments.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even among garments, new flax is forbidden and worn flax, which רבא meant, is allowed.

steps.title: Third praise: keeping purity laws with snow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next praise in the ברייתא: the household of מונבז kept טומאה וטהרה even with snow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They practiced the laws of impurity and purity with snow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last praise of the household of מונבז. This is a setup: the next step brings a source to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא praised them for being careful about טומאה וטהרה with snow. It is not yet clear why that was special. The גמרא will now explain using a משנה about snow.

keyTerms.meaning: the laws of ritual impurity and purity

phrases.english: They practiced impurity and purity with snow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of checking cloths and turns to the third praise in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The household of מונבז was careful about טומאה וטהרה with snow.

steps.title: A משנה on whether snow is food or drink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: snow is neither food nor drink, but if one plans to use it as a drink, it can become impure as a liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Snow is neither food nor drink. If one planned to eat it, it does not become impure as food. If he planned to drink it, it becomes impure as a liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from elsewhere about the status of snow, to explain the praise of the household of מונבז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, snow is not considered food or drink. A person's plan cannot turn it into food. But a plan to use it as a drink does make it count as a liquid for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: he intended, he planned (to use it a certain way)
the impurity that applies to food
the impurity that applies to liquids

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person's plan for an object can change its status for טומאה, but only in one direction here: toward liquid, not toward food.

phrases.english: We learned there:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֶג אֵינוֹ לֹא אוֹכֶל וְלֹא מַשְׁקֶה,
phrases.english: Snow is neither food nor drink.
If he planned to use it for eating,
it does not become impure with the impurity of food;
if he planned it as a drink, it becomes impure with the impurity of liquids.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנן התם שלג אינו לא אוכל ולא משקה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to explain the praise about snow from step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Snow is neither food nor drink. A plan to eat it does not make it food for טומאה, but a plan to drink it makes it a liquid for טומאה.

steps.title: Part of the snow impure, part of the snow pure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if part of the snow becomes טמא, the rest does not. If part of it becomes טהור, all of it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If part of the snow became impure, not all of it became impure. If part of it was purified, all of it is purified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source about snow with two more rules. One rule is about becoming טמא and the other is about becoming טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lump of snow is not treated as one connected thing for טומאה, so only the part that was touched becomes טמא. For טהרה the rule goes the other way: purifying one part, for example when it touches the water of a מקוה, purifies the whole lump.

phrases.english: If part of it became impure, not all of it became impure;
phrases.notes: "It" is the snow from the source quoted just before.

phrases.english: if part of it was purified, all of it is purified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted source about the status of snow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Part of the snow becoming טמא does not make all of it טמא. Part of it becoming טהור makes all of it טהור.

steps.title: The two rules seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the second rule can talk about a fully טמא lump of snow, when the first rule says the whole lump does not become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This source is difficult in itself. You said that if part became impure, not all of it became impure. Then you say that if part is purified, all of it is purified. That implies all of it had become impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from inside its own words. The first half and the second half do not seem to fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about purifying the whole lump only makes sense if the whole lump was טמא to begin with. But the first rule says that touching part of the snow does not make all of it טמא. So how could the entire lump ever have become טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult, meaning it contradicts itself
That is to say; this implies

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying either rule is wrong. It is asking how both can be true at once: how could a whole lump of snow ever become טמא?

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: "If part of it became impure, not all of it became impure,"
and then you say:
phrases.notes: Some versions say "he teaches" (in round brackets); the corrected wording in square brackets says "you say." The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: "If part of it was purified, all of it is purified,"
which implies that all of it had become impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source just quoted by setting its two halves against each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's two rules about snow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second rule assumes the whole lump was טמא. The first rule implies that touching part of it cannot make all of it טמא, so that situation seems impossible.

steps.title: אביי: the snow passed through the airspace of an oven
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the whole lump can become טמא if it is passed through the airspace of a טמא earthenware oven, since everything inside a כלי חרס becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: for example, where one passed the snow through the airspace of an oven, for the Torah testified about an earthenware vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He shows a real case where the entire lump of snow becomes טמא at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule is about something touching part of the snow, and that affects only the part it touches. But a כלי חרס that holds טומאה makes everything in its airspace טמא. So if the whole lump passes through the oven's airspace, the whole lump becomes טמא, and the second rule now makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified; here, the תורה tells us this rule

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס makes things טמא through its airspace, even without touching them. That is how a whole lump of snow can become טמא all at once.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the first rule only limits טומאה that spreads by touching. It does not block טומאה that comes from the airspace of a כלי חרס.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For example, where one passed it through the airspace of an oven,
phrases.notes: He means an earthenware oven that has something טמא inside it.

phrases.english: for the Torah testified about an earthenware vessel

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל אֲוִיר תַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: a special situation in which all the snow becomes טמא at once.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A whole lump of snow could never become טמא, so the rule about purifying all of it seemed to have no case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Passing the snow through the airspace of a טמא כלי חרס makes all of it טמא. In that case, purifying part of it purifies the whole.
